alex: Heads up — production latency spike on model: rwd-8k-v2 at ~11:03 UTC. P95 went from 120ms -> 420ms for text-generation route that normally uses Triton by default. Not seeing GPU saturation.

sara: saw that. Perf traces attached: https://perf.redwood/captures/1769801109 (gputrace + nvprof). Early signal looks like KV-cache hit ratio jumped, and Triton kernel path had a serial fallback causing extra memcpy.

mike: oof. Is this the seqlen-dependent routing we autotuned last month? I remember the autotuner prefers Triton for seq <= 512 on A100 because of better matmul packing. But that assumes cold KV (no massive cache reuse).

jen: adding the trace. Key snippet from profiler: `kernel: triton_gemm_seq128, time: 1.8ms; fallback: cutlass_gemm_seq128_copy, time: 12.4ms`. Fallback occurs when KV cache is active and some workspace allocation fails inside Triton.

alex: so fallback is expensive because we memcpy full KV buffer out/in. That explains the jump even though utilization looked fine. We need to change routing so we don't pick Triton when KV-cache ratio > 70% for seq <= 256.

perf-bot: [alert] route=/v1/generate model=rwd-8k-v2 p95=420ms p50=95ms error_rate=0.3% traces=3 linked_issue=#3421

mike: question — is this specific to A100 40GB or reproducible on 80GB and L40? We should avoid making config that is hardware-specific unless necessary.

sara: repro'd on 40GB and 80GB. L40 shows smaller penalty. Looks like Triton kernel's workspace alloc path uses a allocator that fragments when the KV cache alloc pattern changes. CUTLASS path avoids that.

jen: proposed quick fix (hotpatch): in routing policy add condition: `use_triton = (seq_len >= 384 || kv_cache_active == false) && model_arch in [gpt2, gptj]` — otherwise prefer cutlass. Also add metrics: `kv_cache_active_ratio` to per-route sampling.

alex: sounds good. Can we implement feature-flagged change and roll to canary? Also add autotuner change: include `kv_cache_hit_ratio` and `active_seq_distribution` as features for the tuner. Current tuner only considers seq histogram + arch + batch_size.

mike: agree. I'll open a PR with the routing predicate + unit tests. Also will add a small micro-benchmark that simulates live KV reuse and verifies no memcpy fallback is triggered. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/eng-runtime/pulls/2897

perf-bot: CI perf-run summary: canary 10k reqs, p95 down 38% vs baseline when using cutlass preference on kv-heavy traces.

oncall-bot: paging eng-runtime oncall: @mike, @jen — high-latency alert acknowledged.

jen: noted. I'll prepare rollout plan: canary 5% -> 20% -> 50% with automatic rollback if p95 increases by >10% or errors >1%. Also we should add a regression test to the profiler harness that injects KV cache state into autotuner sims.

alex: thanks team. Action items: mike PR + microbench, jen rollout plan + metrics, sara add kv_cache feature to tuner input, perf-bot keep sampling traces. We'll reconvene if canary trips. :thumbsup:
